items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: “Slingshot, this guy’s banging me in the back all the time.” He says, “Let’s change places.”

ctx.x: I don’t know. But they were very nice to me, and they’d show me, they’d tell me, so that’s why I know about offays, because in one of these places, this was about four in the morning. I’d get through at three, and they’d meet me somewhere down around 125th Street, and we’d go around for a couple of hours. But at the bar, sometimes I was the only white guy there. And these guys would — this one guy’s name was Slingshot. I said,

“Slingshot, this guy’s banging me in the back all the time.” He says, “Let’s change places.” So he got over there, and nobody — so he says, “Listen to them,” and they would torture me, and say, “Hey go on there, rubber band.” He says they’re not talking about nothing, they’re hijiving. Don’t you want to hijive with them? You know, just talking. The rubber means automobile. And they had names for each thing. So he was explaining what they were doing. He said, “They ain’t talking about nothing.
And he said they were hijiving.
